notes.summary: Unverified all-dimensional reconstruction of saturated-normal intersection algebra, genuine real-centre PC/PAPC equivalence, finite rational PC cones and exact real-reference decomposition. These supporting proofs retain the tangential term, actual indices, every ordinary-open real-cycle test and zero repeated-factor rules.
notes.detailedSummary: Direct codimension-two cancellation proves balancing and mixed commutativity in every dimension with real coefficients and actual saturated quotient lattices. Finite rational tangent-family tests characterize PC against every allowed structure and every real centre. Rational local one-cycles prove the PAPC converse without inserting irrational vertices. An active-face rational box decomposes each prescribed positive-growth real reference exactly into rational PC references on unchanged rational spatial domains. Product-normal rules, elementary multivariate convex facts and complete recursive vanishing support n2. No predecessor verdict or external theorem conclusion is granted.
notes.text:
Unverified mathematical supporting result for P05.2 in the explicit real scalar extension on finite rational spatial complexes. No prior theorem, canonical note, catalogue assertion or review is a premise. Original P05.2 remains open.

Conventions follow BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1, manuscript 10 March 2026. Definitions 2.18 and 2.31 use N_sigma=N intersect span_R(sigma-sigma) and a lift n_{sigma/tau} of the primitive inward generator of N_sigma/N_tau. Definitions 3.2–3.3 test Jensen for rational endpoints, arbitrary nonnegative real coefficients summing to one and their actual possibly irrational barycentre, when a permitted rational structure has a common face containing the centre in all endpoint cofaces. Definition 3.1 tests PAPC against every nonnegative local balanced cycle of every positive dimension on every ordinary open. Definition 6.2 uses only h<=gamma+C_h as raw growth. Definition 2.28’s integral slopes and rational constants remain distinct from the declared real coefficients. On a fixed rational complex, affine continuity is a rational linear system, so a rational basis with denominators cleared establishes its real scalar extension. Cycle balancing likewise has rational coefficients.

For real PA h and balanced real k-cycle z define
D_h z(tau)=sum_{sigma>tau}z(sigma)h_sigma^lin(n_{sigma/tau})−h_tau^lin(sum_{sigma>tau}z(sigma)n_{sigma/tau}).
The second argument is tangential. Changes of normal lift cancel because the affine pieces agree on tau. The formula is bilinear, local and zero for ambient real affine functions.

Refinement follows by inspecting the minimal old face of a tested new (k−1)-face. If its dimension exceeds k, all incident inherited k-weights vanish. If its dimension is k, precisely two pieces in that inherited k-plane have potentially nonzero inherited weights; their weights and linear parts agree and their primitive quotient classes are opposite. Other incident pieces have zero weights. If its dimension is k−1, locally one inherited incident k-piece corresponds to each old incident k-face, with unchanged saturated tangent and primitive normal class. These cases prove inherited balancing and divisor refinement. Applying them at every stage gives zero top coefficient at any newly inserted zero-face that was not an old zero-face.

For balancing and commutativity fix a (k−2)-face theta, translate its germ, subtract an ambient real extension of each common tangential linear part and quotient by N_theta. This lattice is saturated. N_sigma/N_theta is saturated in N/N_theta: if mn+t belongs to N_sigma with t in N_theta, then mn belongs to N_sigma, hence n belongs to N_sigma. Thus quotient normals remain actual primitive normals. Incident cones contain span(theta) as common lineality; quotienting preserves intersections because two lifts of a common quotient point differ by that lineality. Rational cuts make the resulting two-cones pointed without changing divisors.

For primitive bounding rays r,s put chi_rs=[N_cone:Zr+Zs] and omega_rs equal to the actual cone weight. Extending r to a basis of the saturated plane lattice shows that s/chi_rs represents its primitive inward quotient class. Its discrepancy from an integral lift is tangential and cancels. Balancing at r and its first-divisor coefficient are
sum_s(omega_rs/chi_rs)s=t_r r,
D_h(r)=sum_s(omega_rs/chi_rs)h(s)−t_rh(r).
Here functions are homogeneous after subtraction. In sum_r D_h(r)r, interchange r and s in the first double sum; it becomes sum_r h(r)sum_s(omega_rs/chi_rs)s, exactly the subtracted sum. The first divisor is balanced. For a second homogeneous function g the complete coefficient is
sum_{unordered {r,s}}(omega_rs/chi_rs)[h(s)g(r)+h(r)g(s)]−sum_r t_rh(r)g(r).
Both terms are symmetric. The tangential term is retained. This proves mixed commutativity at every theta and in every k; adjacent transpositions give every mixed order. For k=1 the resulting zero-cycle has no balancing condition. Every recursive intermediate cycle is therefore balanced. These arguments directly handle real coefficients and weights; positivity is proved separately.

For product cycles, saturated tangent lattices split as direct sums. A facet lowers exactly one factor, with its actual primitive normal embedded as (n,0) and the other inherited weight as multiplier. Consequently a pulled-back function has divisor (h.z) times the other cycle. At facets lowering another factor, its normal evaluation and tangential correction vanish. This holds for every intermediate tensor cycle. On a zero-dimensional exhausted factor the restricted function is constant, so another divisor from it vanishes. Actual indices are retained. Nonsaturation of the whole star’s ray-generated span does not change the split saturated product planes.

The finite-dimensional facts used below have elementary proofs. Remove rational lineality from a finitely defined rational cone. In its pointed quotient the sum of its nonnegative defining forms is positive away from zero. Its value-one section is bounded: otherwise a normalized unbounded sequence would yield a nonzero cone vector of value zero. A bounded polyhedron is the convex hull of its finitely many vertices: a line through a nonvertex in its minimal face reaches smaller faces, and induction reduces dimension. Vertices solve full-rank active systems and are rational for rational data. Lift back and add both signs of a rational lineality basis. Homogenization gives every nonempty pointed rational polyhedron as the convex hull of finitely many rational vertices plus the cone of finitely many rational recession generators. It has a vertex because its homogenized cone needs a positive-height generator. The real-data version holds without coordinate rationality. Eliminating a variable compares every lower bound with every upper bound and keeps independent inequalities; one-sided bounds impose none. Repetition proves polyhedral projection and closedness of finite convex-hull-plus-cone sets, retaining rational variable coefficients even with real constants.

On a fixed finite rational complex Sigma, continuous affine assignments form a rational vector space A. For every face tau and coface sigma, and every real y in relint(tau), T_{tau,sigma}=cone(sigma−y) is the rational tangent cone defined by homogeneous equalities and precisely the inequalities active on tau. A nonnegative affine inequality on tau can vanish at a relative-interior point only if identically zero there. Inactive inequalities have positive slack, so each direction satisfying the active system admits a sufficiently small positive feasible step. This proves independence of y, closedness, rationality and inclusion of all tangential lineality.

Let B_tau consist of families d_sigma in T_{tau,sigma} with sum d_sigma=0, including the tau slot. It has finitely many rational generators, retaining both signs of rational lineality. Impose sum h_sigma^lin(d_sigma)>=0 on every generator. Necessity for PC uses rational y and rational endpoints y+m epsilon d_sigma with equal coefficients 1/m and sufficiently small rational epsilon. For sufficiency, these tests make successive slopes nondecreasing along every contained straight segment, including at real breakpoints. Thus h is convex along each such segment. For a PCC on any other structure, each centre-to-endpoint segment lies in the carrier. Its endpoint increment is at least its initial derivative. Group weighted initial directions in the fixed tangent cones; their sum is zero, so the tests give Jensen. Zero displacements contribute zero. This proves actual PC at all real centres, on all permitted structures and with remote rational endpoints. The resulting cone C in A is a finite rational homogeneous cone.

PC implies every PAPC test in dimensions 1,…,d. At a tested facet inside an ordinary open choose rational x in its relative interior. Nonnegative balanced incident vectors form a rational polyhedral cone, so it suffices to test rational generators c_sigma. Write S=sum c_sigma>0 and T=sum c_sigma n_{sigma/tau}, rational and tangential. For sufficiently small rational epsilon, endpoints x+epsilon(n_{sigma/tau}−T/S) lie in their actual cells and open, with barycentre x and coefficients c_sigma/S. Jensen multiplied by S/epsilon is exactly the divisor inequality. The zero vector gives zero, and positive real combinations give every real test.

Conversely PAPC implies the tangent-family tests. Write each nonzero rational generator direction d_sigma=a_sigma n_sigma with positive rational a_sigma and primitive integral ray n_sigma. At rational y place these weights on short initial rays inside the actual cofaces, adding weights on coincident rays. A small ordinary ball excludes their rational outer endpoints. This is a local one-cycle because sum d_sigma=0; other subdivision points are bivalent with equal opposite weights. Finite rational ambient hyperplane cuts include the segments and y as allowed faces. PAPC at y is the generator inequality. The preceding finite-cone sufficiency then proves genuine PC at every real centre, without inserting an irrational centre as a rational vertex.

Exact reference decomposition follows. For prescribed gamma in C positive at infinity, cells are pointed because nonzero lineality would require opposite affine slopes both positive. Finite recession generators supply finitely many strict rational linear inequalities. Intersect the kernels of exactly the PC inequalities active at gamma; this is a rational subspace S. A small relative ball around gamma in S stays in C because every other inequality is strict. It spans S and is the relative interior of the minimal face: a point of that face can be paired with a short opposite step from gamma to express gamma as a strict convex combination. Choose a rational coordinate box enclosing gamma inside that ball and retaining every strict recession inequality. Its rational vertices gamma_a are actual-PC rational references on the unchanged spatial complex. Positive product barycentric weights give gamma=sum lambda_a gamma_a exactly, with sum lambda_a=1. The zero-dimensional case allows gamma=0 only if the strict recession conditions are empty. No approximation or changed reference occurs.

On graphs the tangent tests are exactly edgewise convexity and c.s_v>=0 for every c in K_v, including all opposite-pair relations at higher-rank vertices and bivalent bends. For any finite number of factor-PC functions, product tangent cones are products: finitely many projected directions admit a common small feasible step. Project and group a sum-zero product tangent family in each factor. Each factor gives a nonnegative derivative sum; their sum gives product PC. This includes zero projections and every real centre and does not assume projected remote cofaces form an allowed factor structure.

For a proper ambient rational norm rho centred at a rational point, the pointed-cell decomposition gives gamma_a>=m_a rho−Q_a with rational m_a>0,Q_a>=0. Choose m_a below every positive reference recession-slope/rho_0 ratio. Affinity bounds the vertex term below; the norm triangle inequality bounds it above; finitely many vertex bounds give Q_a. Every cell, component and end is included.

A finite rational Jensen function on Q^m has a continuous convex completion. Corner values bound it above on rational boxes; reflection about a rational centre bounds it below on smaller boxes. Extending a short rational segment by a rational factor within the larger box bounds the difference by a constant times its length. This gives local Lipschitz completion, and density proves convexity. A finite convex function has an affine support at every point: separate points approaching its epigraph from below using nearest-point normals, whose vertical coefficient is positive since the domain is all R^m; normalize, bound slopes using values at x±Re_i and pass to a convergent subsequence. Nearest-point separation also separates a disjoint compact polytope and closed cone. A polytope’s outward normal cone is generated by active inequality normals, because an extra normal could be separated to give a feasible improving direction. For b(p)=min_i(c_i+g_i.p), the supergradient polytope is the convex hull of active gradients, by its minimum directional derivative and separation. Nonnegative sums give Minkowski supergradient sums, including zero coefficients.

Two complete-recursion vanishing principles are needed. If, after ambient affine subtraction, a germ on a d-cycle factors through a rational map to a complete rational fan of dimension q<d, its j-th divisor is supported above target faces of codimension at least j. Initially it is affine off the walls. Near a target face of codimension j−1, the preceding cycle is supported in that face’s preimage and the function is affine on its supporting subspace. Extend this affine function; balancing makes the next divisor zero there. Induction gives zero after q+1 slots, including all lower faces. If carrier and residual function fans have common nonzero rational lineality, a common fan retaining it has no zero-face; the top divisor vanishes and refinement preserves the zero.

For PAPC P the successive divisors are balanced and nonnegative, and its top measure is the finite zero-cycle on old structure vertices, as in BMPS Definition 4.4. P+1/n decreases uniformly in gamma+O(1), with identical measures since constants have zero divisors. No diffuse, escaping or infinity term is introduced. Total reference mass is preserved: P^d−gamma^d=(P−gamma).sum_{i=0}^{d−1}P^i gamma^{d−1−i}.[X]. The inner balanced one-cycle has bounded-edge slope cancellation and zero end slope for the bounded difference. This identity does not establish contact.

The complete supporting arguments and essential selected primary bodies, including Allermann–Rau arXiv:0709.3705v3 Definition 3.1–Proposition 3.7, are directly included in P05.2-argument.md. Its integral source convention is separated from the independently proved real extension and actual-index applications. Rerun python3 snapshot_sources.py; python3 diagnostics.py; python3 compose_argument.py; python3 build.py. These are unverified mathematical drafts; source hashes, execution, compilation and prior reviews do not establish correctness.

notes.summary: Unverified finite-product classification for every d>=2 and each prescribed positive-growth real reference with actual positive real weights: regularizable rational-domain PAPC raw envelopes and complete contact for all bounded real-PA obstacles occur iff every factor’s local relation cone has rank one and at most one factor branches. Both failures give exact PAPC envelopes and complete negative integrals. Original P05.2 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1, componentwise rational weight ratios reduce the positive case to graph-times-affine components. The full multivariate partial-Legendre incidence construction retains nonseparable data, rational spatial domains despite real dual chambers, all cycle edges and every noncontact stratum. Higher-rank factors yield intrinsic proper-support caps with fibrewise rational raw pinning and complete integral −d!(delta epsilon M) product_{j>=2}(2delta b_jw_j). Two rank-one branching factors yield a tripod tensor obstruction; apex-fibre PCCs and uniformly available rational radial outer points pin the whole bump. Complete intermediate-cycle formulas give −(d!/2!)8kappa^2ab product_{j>=3}(2kappa b_jw_j). Homogeneous germ support and zero refinement coefficients establish both complete integrals. This is a special-case draft, not closure of the original atom.
notes.text:
Unverified unconditional special-case theorem for P05.2. Let d>=2 and X=product_{j=1}^d G_j for nonempty finite embedded balanced rational pure graphs with actual saturated lattices and arbitrary positive actual real edge weights. Retain all components, bounded edges, cycles, full lines and ends. Fix EACH prescribed continuous rational-domain real-PA actual-PC gamma positive on every nonzero affine-cell recession vector. For this fixed reference, every bounded continuous rational-domain real-PA obstacle has a finite continuous rational-domain actual-PAPC true raw envelope in gamma+O(1), uniform decreasing PAPC regularization and COMPLETE d-stage contact integral zero if and only if all local nonnegative relation cones have rank one and at most ONE factor is branched. The operator is P^d.[X], without division by d!. This closes only the specified finite-product family. Original P05.2 remains open; candidate=false.

This note uses n1’s directly proved all-dimensional primitive-normal algebra, refinement/locality, product rules, genuine PC/PAPC equivalence, finite PC cones, elementary convex facts and recursive vanishing. No earlier verdict, book assertion or external theorem conclusion is otherwise a premise. The complete dependency chain and selected primary bodies are included in P05.2-argument.md.

Positive geometry and actual weights. At a rank-one vertex span K_v equals the full rational direction kernel: perturbing the strictly positive actual weight vector in both directions realizes every kernel vector. Thus its sole relation has a positive primitive integer generator. Incident weight ratios are rational. Propagate from one edge through each connected component; the given actual weights guarantee consistency around cycles. Actual weights are c times positive rational r_e, with c>0 real. Bivalent directions are opposite primitive vectors with equal weights. A rank-one branching vertex has no opposite pair, which would provide another relation. Each unbranched component is a whole rational affine line: bivalent propagation stays on that line, a finite endpoint would be one-valent and unbalanced, and an embedded bounded cycle cannot lie in the line. With at most one branching factor, each product component is G times a complete rational affine space E of dimension m=d−1. The actual lattice splits into the graph lattice and primitive line lattices. Its initial cycle is one positive real scalar times the rationally weighted cylinder cycle. Linearity in the initial cycle multiplies the entire recursive measure by that scalar once, leaving the envelope and contact unchanged.

The complete multivariate cylinder construction follows. A finite function on rational graph points satisfying rational-coefficient graph PCCs has a continuous edgewise-convex completion. Endpoint chords give finite one-sided limits at most the specified endpoint value. Small rational vertex PCCs with coefficients r_e/sum r_e force all limits to equal that value. Dividing those inequalities by distance gives finite outgoing derivatives and sum r_e s_e>=0: each derivative has a finite upper secant bound, and a negative infinity derivative would violate the weighted inequality. Conversely such k plus any real affine p.z is actual cylinder PC. A permitted convex coface projects into a straight chain or one branch, since a segment cannot traverse a branching rank-one junction without an opposite pair. At a branching centre group displacements t_i q_e with coefficients alpha_i. The resulting b_e=sum alpha_i t_i form a nonnegative relation, hence b_e=c r_e. Edge support inequalities give sum alpha_i(k(q_i)−k(v))>=c sum r_e s_e>=0. Affine E terms cancel, including zero projections, remote endpoints and every real centre.

For finite raw h<=f=gamma+u, define k_{h,p}(q)=inf_{z in E_Q}(h(q,z)−p.z) on rational graph points. Rational graph PCC coefficients allow rational z_i approaching endpoint infima, and their product PCC gives the graph inequality for this infimum. A negative infinity endpoint is handled by varying it alone. Finiteness at one rational graph point propagates throughout its component: an interior finite centre can include any same-edge rational endpoint in a rational PCC; at a finite vertex every incident rational endpoint can be included with positive rational coefficients proportional to r_e/t_e. A finite centre precludes a negative infinity endpoint. This propagates through all cycles and ends, permitting the scalar completion.

Take a common finite rational affine structure for gamma and f, refined by edge strips and split full lines. Its cells are pointed by strict reference recession growth. Let D={p in E*:p.r_E<=s_f(r) for every vertical cell recession generator r}. Bounded u has zero recession slope, so these are also the reference constraints. D contains zero in its interior. For p in D, F_p(q)=inf_{z real}(f(q,z)−p.z) is finite and attained at a vertex of a cell fibre. Fibres are pointed and their recession vectors are generated by vertical cell rays, because end graph recession has only one sign. The objective is nonnegative on them, so the vertex/ray decomposition gives attainment. Outside D a violating rational ray based at a rational point gives negative infinity at a rational graph point. At fixed rational q, finitely many pieces give f(q,z)<=M||z||+B; dual norm ||p||>M makes the infimum negative infinity. Thus D is compact.

Subdivide graph edges at the rational projections of all spatial vertices. Between successive nodes, a fibre vertex lies on a traversing spatial one-face, since slicing its minimal face lowers dimension by at most one. Its trace is z(t)=z_i+t b_i with rational z_i,b_i, and feasibility changes only at projected vertices. Hence F_p(t)=min_i(A_i(p)+t B_i(p)), with finite p-independent indices, real constants and rational p-gradients. Node caps have the same form. Finite candidate endpoint limits give liminf>=F_p(v); fixing finite z and using f continuity gives limsup<=f(v,z)−p.z, then its infimum. Interval formulas therefore extend continuously and concavely to nodes. On final tails theta_e(p)=min_i B_i(p) is the asymptotic slope, and F_p(t)−t theta_e(p) is nondecreasing.

For each p impose the finite incidence system
 a_v<=F_p(v),
 L_v=sum_{bounded e=vw}(r_e/ell_e)(a_w−a_v)+sum_{tails at v}r_e theta_e(p)>=0,
with actual rational primitive lengths and every cycle edge. It is feasible: the finite partial infimum of gamma−||u|| is scalar PC. Replace it by endpoint chords on bounded edges and endpoint lines of slope theta_e on tails. Convexity raises outgoing slopes, concavity of F_p keeps chords below it, and tail monotonicity keeps tail lines below. Coordinatewise maxima preserve feasibility. Maximizing sum a_v in the compact box between a feasible witness and the caps yields a coordinatewise greatest vector a(p), since an exceeding feasible coordinate would improve the maximum by coordinatewise maximum. Its chord/tail interpolation k_p is scalar PC, lies below F_p and dominates every finite k_{h,p} below F_p by the same replacements.

Expand the caps and tail minima into finite inequalities. This is a linear system in (a,p) with rational variable coefficients and real constants. Eliminate other node values by explicit lower/upper-bound comparison. Uniformly lowering all nodes preserves feasibility, so each projected section is (−infinity,a_v(p)]. Its inequalities are upper bounds, giving a_v(p)=min_i(c_{v,i}+g_{v,i}.p) with rational gradients. Tail slopes have the same property. Both are continuous on all of D.

Set Q(q,z)=sup_{p in D}(k_p(q)+p.z). It is finite, actual PC and <=f. At rational (q,z), a touching support p of the rational convex slice of raw h gives h(q,z)=k_{h,p}(q)+p.z. Finiteness propagates, and a violating rational recession ray precludes p outside D. Greatest assignment gives h<=Q. Partition D into finite compact common chambers of the affine minima. Their vertices J may be real; the objective is affine in p on each chamber. Thus Q is a finite real-affine maximum over J on each strip, consistent at nodes and continuous. Rational enclosing simplices in each real point’s minimal rational face extend h<=Q without raw continuity. Applying this to gamma−||u|| gives gamma−||u||<=Q<=f<=gamma+||u||. Q is itself a raw upper-growth competitor, so the actual envelope is Q.

Rational spatial domains require more than that real affine maximum. At p_0 in J let A_v be the supergradient polytope of a_v, B_e that of theta_e and N_D the outward normal cone. Their vertices or generators are rational even when p_0 is real. The maximizer condition is z in −partial^+b(p_0)+N_D: sufficiency is the support/normal inequality; necessity follows by separating the compact translated supergradient polytope from the normal cone to obtain a feasible strictly improving direction. On a bounded interval its domain is z in −(1−t/ell)A_v−(t/ell)A_w+N_D, the convex hull of rational endpoint-column vertices plus rational vertical normal rays. On a tail it is t>=0, z in −A_v−tB_e+N_D, generated by rational base-column points, rays (1,−Vert B_e) and vertical normal rays. These formulas hold at zero coefficients and boundaries. Domains meet in equality faces and glue at nodes because their fibre domain −A_v+N_D is identical. All vertices lie over graph nodes; open-edge and remote-tail zero-faces are excluded. By n1, Q is PAPC and Q+1/n provides the required regularization.

At a possible noncontact atom x=(v,z_0), z_0 is rational. Its compact exposed dual face C_x={p in D:a_v(p)+p.z_0=P(x)} is convex, with rational affine-hull direction since its defining normals are g_{v,i}+z_0. On it a_v is affine. The outgoing functions s_e=(a_w−a_v)/ell_e or theta_e are continuous concave polyhedral and satisfy sum r_e s_e>=0. The exact local germ is h_e(t,zeta)=max_{p in C_x}(p.zeta+t s_e(p)). Inactive finite planes have a positive gap and remain inactive; each p in C_x is a convex combination of common-chamber vertices that must also be active.

If dim C_x<m, its rational direction has a nonzero rational annihilator T in E. Subtract p_0.z. The function and carrier have common T lineality. Coarsest linearity cones are convex unions of finite rational tangent cones and are rational; their equations retain T. Complete recursive lineality vanishing gives zero top coefficient. If dim C_x=m, each interior p has a dual ball p+eta B inside C_x, giving P(v,y)−p.y>=P(x)−p.z_0+eta||y−z_0||. Continuous f(v,y)−p.y attains its infimum. Equality a_v(p)=F_p(v) would force its minimum at z_0 and contact, a contradiction. Thus the cap is strict. If L_v>0, raise only a_v slightly; its strict cap and Laplacian persist and neighbour Laplacians increase, contradicting greatest assignment. With no bounded incident edges, the same increase changes no Laplacian and already contradicts the strict cap. Therefore sum r_e s_e=0 on C_x by continuity. Positive weights and concavity force each s_e affine, since their nonnegative Jensen deficits sum to zero. Their gradients are rational on a full-dimensional chamber interior. Write s_e=alpha_e+p.beta_e. The sole star relation gives a real form A and rational map B with A(q_e)=alpha_e and B(q_e)=beta_e. The whole germ is A(s)+support_{C_x}(zeta+B(s)); after affine subtraction it factors through the rational map to the m-dimensional complete rational normal fan of C_x. Complete quotient vanishing makes its d=m+1 coefficient zero. This covers all cyclic nodes, inserted nodes, fibre walls, tail bases and open-edge strata. Every noncontact coefficient vanishes, so the full finite measure is supported on contact. Apply componentwise and restore the actual scalar to obtain the positive implication.

For both negative cases localize against the prescribed reference on the ENTIRE original product. Use gamma=sum lambda_a gamma_a and gamma_a>=m_a rho−Q_a from n1. For rational-coefficient rational-domain actual-PC F<=Lrho+A choose rational 0<delta_a<m_a/L and large rational C_a. Put P_a=max(gamma_a,C_a+delta_a F), P=sum lambda_a P_a. Each maximum is actual PC with rational walls; the positive real sum retains their common rational domains. Coercivity proves P=gamma outside a compact set on all components and P>=gamma. It is actual PAPC with identical-measure regularization P+1/n. All localizers dominate near the rational centre. Choose a common rational hyperplane structure Pi and insert o as a product vertex. A sufficiently small rational norm ball stays in the common homogeneous germ, misses all other endpoints, bends, nonincident cells and hyperplanes not through o. Every remaining constraint is homogeneous. Each nonzero point admits a short radial contraction and expansion inside its minimal face; o is the only old zero-face in that ball.

Higher relations. Suppose G_1 has rank>=2 at v, with directions q_i and actual weights w_i. The rational pointed relation cone has an extreme generator c with nonempty proper support I: a strictly positive extreme vector could be perturbed in both directions of an independent kernel vector, contradicting extremality. Set s_i=0 on I and 1 elsewhere. Then c.s=0, every nonnegative relation pairs nonnegatively with s, and M=sum w_i s_i>0. Choose rational edge-interior y_j in every other graph, actual primitive r_j and actual weight w_j>0. Put b_j=||r_j||_1. Along first rays rho_1(v+tq_i)=a_i t, a_i=||q_i||_1. Choose rational 0<epsilon<min a_i, rational short lengths L_i before existing endpoints and breakpoints, and 0<A<min L_i(a_i−epsilon s_i). Replace the norm on the star by F_1=max(a_i t,A+epsilon s_i t), glued back to rho_1 elsewhere. Comparison points A/(a_i−epsilon s_i) are rational and inside the star. Central slopes satisfy every intrinsic relation test; new bends increase to a_i. Thus F_1 is genuine intrinsic PC without an ambient extension of s, and 0<=F_1−rho_1<=A. Product tangent families give F=F_1+sum_{j>=2}rho_j global actual PC. Localization gives the exact germ
P=C+delta epsilon s_i t+sum_{j>=2}delta b_j|z_j|,
where delta=sum lambda_a delta_a>0. Gamma is unchanged at infinity.

Choose rational B<T and widths D_j with max a_i T+sum b_jD_j<r_0. On the short star put beta=(1−t/B−sum|z_j|/D_j)_+, zero elsewhere, and u=P−gamma+beta. This is a nonnegative compact bounded continuous rational-domain real-PA obstacle with beta(o)=1. For every rational extra tuple z, endpoints (v+Tq_i,z), i in I, with coefficients c_i/sum c_i form a genuine coarse product PCC whose common face is the entire fibre over v. They are rational and have zero bump. Since c.s=0, any raw q<=P+beta has q(v,z)<=P(v,z). Rational segment interpolation between this apex and the point at T bounds all rational ray segments. Outside beta the ceiling bounds directly. Rational enclosing boxes in each minimal local ray/sign face then bound every real centre exactly, including t=0 and every zero extra displacement, using P affinity. No raw continuity or irrational endpoints are used. Elsewhere beta=0. P itself is a global competitor, so the true raw envelope equals P everywhere.

The factor divisors are m_1=delta epsilon M at the first star origin and m_j=2delta b_jw_j at each other primitive line origin. They use actual primitive outgoing vectors and actual weights. Product quotient normals are these factor primitives, with split indices one even if the whole first-star ray span is nonsaturated. For every r, the COMPLETE intermediate cycle of (sum h_j)^r is r! times the sum over subsets of r distinct factors of their zero-divisors times the remaining one-cycles. Word expansion and the actual product-normal rule prove this: repeated exhausted factors vanish, and every order of distinct factors gives the same tensor. Consequently the full d-stage origin mass is
d! (delta epsilon M) product_{j>=2}(2delta b_jw_j)>0.
Every intermediate stratum and every ordering is included.

Two branches. Suppose all local cones have rank one but G_1,G_2 branch at v_1,v_2. Write actual incident weights a ell_i,b m_j, with primitive positive integer relations ell,m and actual real scales a,b>0. Partition each star into three nonempty groups I_k,J_k.
